ops.rationale: The Abstract says the hand-crafted features have the highest ARI at the 9:1 ratio, ahead of ECGFounder with the values of Section 4.6, in place of 'keep', which misstated the direction of the result.
ops.new_text:
\begin{abstract}
Unsupervised analysis of the electrocardiogram (ECG) promises label-free
discovery of cardiac structure, yet whether clustering succeeds depends less on
the algorithm than on how the signal is represented. We benchmark four
representation families for unsupervised separation of sinus rhythm (SR) from
atrial fibrillation (AF) on PTB-XL: \rev{whole-record} raw flattening, a convolutional
\rev{autoencoder (conv-AE)}, compact hand-crafted rhythm and morphology features,
and two frozen foundation-model embeddings (HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder).
Evaluation is chance-corrected (adjusted Rand index, ARI), patient-grouped,
\rev{repeated over ten seeds for the clusterers that depend on one}, and bounded by a
supervised ceiling\rev{, the accuracy a supervised probe reaches on the same features}. ECGFounder clusters
best (ARI up to 0.885), but 16 interpretable hand-crafted features are competitive
(0.711) and far ahead of the raw and \rev{conv-AE} pipelines (ARI $\approx 0$)\rev{.
Both match a majority-class assignment, the conv-AE despite a supervised ceiling of 0.678
and the raw pipeline with a ceiling of 0.519 against a majority of 0.504.}
The same ordering holds on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task. Two cautions emerge: the
silhouette score rewards the degenerate one-cluster solution (silhouette 0.81 at
ARI \rev{0.000}) and cannot validate ECG clustering alone, and \rev{feature scaling, the
per-feature transformation applied before clustering, moves the mean ARI of the
hand-crafted features from 0.229 to 0.629 across four scalers.
The chance-corrected controls locate where naive pipelines fail.
Under heavy class imbalance, at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio, the hand-crafted features have the
highest ARI, ahead of ECGFounder (0.265 against 0.063).
Under federation across ten sites that differ in class prevalence they retain the largest
share of their centralized ARI, 0.92 against 0.69 for ECGFounder, at about one fifteenth
of its inference time per record.}
\end{abstract}

ops.rationale: The citations of sslclustering2025 and lookingbeyond2026 take the wording citation-report.md gives as supported (C20, C3, C4): one image-encoder study, and an ARI analysis pooled over four 12-lead datasets with no hand-crafted baseline and no MIT-BIH.
ops.new_text:
A representation can carry information about a label and still fail to cluster by it.
Linear separability and clusterability are distinct properties: a representation may
place the discriminative direction far from its dominant axes of variation, so that a
supervised probe recovers the label while an unsupervised partition does not.
\rev{Representations with nearly the same linear-evaluation accuracy can differ in how well
they cluster, as reported for self-supervised image encoders \cite{sslclustering2025}.
We treat the distinction as background.} What
has not been measured, for ECG, is how the common representation families compare on
this axis under proper chance-corrected metrics.
\rev{The most directly related work compares four ECG foundation models with one another
and with no hand-crafted baseline \cite{lookingbeyond2026}. It includes a
cluster-separability analysis (adjusted Rand index) of embeddings drawn from four 12-lead
datasets, PTB-XL among them. Those datasets do not include the MIT-BIH database.}
\rev{This study adds both: a hand-crafted arm built from RR-interval and beat-morphology
features \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, and a beat-morphology task on the MIT-BIH
Arrhythmia Database \cite{mitbih2001}.}

ops.rationale: Contribution (iii) says the hand-crafted features have the highest ARI at the 9:1 ratio and retain the largest share under non-IID federation, in place of 'keep the highest', which ECGFounder's balanced-data lead contradicts.
ops.new_text:
We therefore benchmark four representation families for unsupervised SR-versus-AF
separation \rev{(sinus rhythm versus atrial fibrillation)}, with the controls the original
pipeline lacked. \rev{Because SR and AF differ by definition in the regularity of the
rhythm, it is expected that compact hand-crafted features and a large foundation model
both recover the split.
The ordering of the representations is therefore not the contribution.
What the benchmark adds is what the controls reveal and how the representations behave
under deployment stress.} Our contributions are modest and empirical\rev{:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] A chance-corrected, patient-grouped and significance-tested clustering
benchmark of raw, convolutional autoencoder (conv-AE), hand-crafted, and two frozen
foundation-model representations. Patient-grouped means that no patient appears in more
than one fold. Each representation is bounded by a supervised ceiling, the accuracy a
supervised probe reaches on the same features, and the comparison is shown stable across
the assumed number of clusters.
\item[(ii)] Two reproducible methodological cautions that explain the original project's
misleading numbers. Internal validity indices such as the silhouette, which are computed
without labels, reward the degenerate collapse. Feature scaling, the per-feature
transformation applied to a representation before clustering (Yeo-Johnson power,
standard, quantile or robust scaling), changes the result by a wide margin.
\item[(iii)] The behaviour of the representations under two independent deployment
stressors: heavy class imbalance, and federation across sites that differ in class
proportions (non-IID). The 16 hand-crafted features have the highest adjusted Rand index
(ARI) at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio and retain the largest share of their centralized ARI under
non-IID federation.
\item[(iv)] A generalization check on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task, the dataset the
closest prior benchmark omits.
\end{enumerate}
\end{revblock}
We do not propose a new method. \rev{The statements about foundation models concern
HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder, the two evaluated here, and the
separability-versus-clusterability phenomenon is credited to prior work.}

ops.rationale: The contrastive-methods sentence takes the wording C7 gives as supported by its three sources, and the scope sentence names this study's arm 'the conv-AE' in place of 'a reconstruction autoencoder'.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Unsupervised ECG and representations.} Hand-crafted features built from
RR-interval irregularity and beat morphology encode the defining signatures of common
arrhythmias and underpin decades of automatic analysis \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}.
Tensor and wavelet decompositions have been combined with spectral clustering for
unsupervised 12-lead classification \cite{wavelettensorecg2018}. \rev{A reconstruction
autoencoder is trained to reproduce its input and receives no class information, so
nothing in its objective arranges its code by class.} \rev{Contrastive self-supervised
methods built on physiologically motivated augmentations and patient- or lead-level
invariances, including CLOCS \cite{clocs2021}, 3KG \cite{threekg2021} and contrastive
predictive coding for 12-lead ECG \cite{mehari2022ssl}, learn ECG representations without
labels.} Self-supervised and foundation models for
ECG, such as HuBERT-ECG \cite{hubertecg2024} and ECGFounder \cite{ecgfounder2024}, learn
general representations from millions of recordings and are now evaluated as frozen
feature extractors. The wavelet-tensor and spectral-clustering pipeline of
\cite{wavelettensorecg2018} addresses a related unsupervised goal with a different
(tensor) representation\rev{. This study focuses on four families, which range from
representations shaped only by signal energy, raw flattening and the conv-AE, to features
built from the defining signatures of the classes, and include two frozen foundation
embeddings. A tensor arm is left to future work.}

ops.rationale: The closest-benchmark paragraph takes the wording C5 gives: the ARI was computed on embeddings pooled over four 12-lead datasets, PTB-XL among them.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{Closest benchmark.} \rev{The ECG foundation-model benchmark of
\cite{lookingbeyond2026} reported cluster-separability (ARI) of foundation-model
embeddings pooled over four 12-lead datasets, PTB-XL among them. In that analysis some
models clustered by clinical label while others clustered by dataset. It compared
foundation models to one another and stated that prior work omits a representation-wise
evaluation. It did not add a hand-crafted baseline, and it did not include MIT-BIH. Beyond
these two additions, this study adds a supervised ceiling so that a low clustering score
can be attributed to geometry rather than to missing information.}

ops.rationale: Under the Decision on C6 the counts 21 799 and 18 869 are given as those of the version 1.0.3 release and no longer attributed to ptbxl2020, which is cited for the database; the likelihood-zero statement gets the citation C34 found in that paper.
ops.new_text:
\paragraph{PTB-XL.} \rev{We used PTB-XL \cite{ptbxl2020}, a public database of 10\,s
12-lead records, in its version 1.0.3 release, which holds 21\,799 records from 18\,869
patients. Rhythm labels were taken
from the SCP-ECG (Standard Communications Protocol for Computer-Assisted
Electrocardiography) statements. The SR-versus-AF cohort used as positives all records
carrying an AF statement, atrial fibrillation (AFIB) or atrial flutter (AFLT), so that both
count as AF, and as controls the sinus-rhythm records without any AF statement.}
PTB-XL encodes rhythm statements at a likelihood of zero meaning ``present'' \rev{\cite{ptbxl2020}},
\rev{so a presence-based rule was required, since a confidence threshold would have
discarded every SR record. We drew} a balanced, patient-disjoint cohort of 2\,542 records
(1\,282 SR, 1\,260 AF), so the majority-class baseline is 0.504. \rev{Records were read
from the WFDB-format files of the \mbox{100\,Hz} release of the database and converted once
to a single-precision floating-point array of 1000 samples by 12 leads. No filtering,
resampling or rescaling was applied before each representation's own preprocessing, so
every representation started from the same array. The lead set and any further
preprocessing were chosen per representation rather than once for the whole study, and
are stated with each representation below.} All evaluation \rev{was} patient-grouped: no
patient appears in more than one fold or in both classes.

ops.rationale: The Representations subsection gets a label so that the Limitations can point at it; the heading text is unchanged.
ops.new_text: \subsection{Representations}\label{sec:representations}

ops.rationale: The clifford2017af sentence says what the source is, a classification challenge for AF detection from a single short lead (C21), in place of 'the established setting'; the challenge's team count is left out because main.tex holds no such number.
ops.new_text:
We compare four families on PTB-XL (Table~\ref{tab:main})\rev{:}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Raw flattening} reproduces the original pipeline: each lead \rev{was}
moving-average downsampled and all leads \rev{were} concatenated into one vector
($\sim$2000 dimensions). It carries amplitude and energy but no \rev{cross-record}
temporal alignment. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, 1000 samples by 12 leads. A
non-overlapping six-sample mean per lead left 166 samples per lead and a
1992-dimensional vector. This arm treats the sample amplitudes as the features and
imposes no clinical model on the signal. All twelve leads entered because the arm
reproduces the originating pipeline, which concatenated every lead.}
\item \textbf{Convolutional autoencoder} (conv-AE): a 1-D convolutional autoencoder
with a 32-unit bottleneck, trained to convergence with a validation split. This is a
properly specified reconstruction model, in contrast to the original collapsed dense
autoencoder. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, resampled to 12 by 2500 and z-scored per lead.
A reconstruction objective compresses whatever carries signal energy, which need not be
what separates the classes.}
\item \textbf{Hand-crafted} (16 features): RR-interval statistics and irregularity
\rev{(the standard deviation of the RR intervals (SDNN), the root mean square of successive
RR differences (RMSSD), the proportion of successive RR differences above \mbox{50\,ms}
(pNN50), the coefficient of variation, RR entropy and mean heart rate)}, P-wave
presence and amplitude, QRS width and amplitude, and beat-template consistency\rev{,
[GAP: one-clause definition of beat-template consistency, from the study's feature
extraction]} \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, extracted with NeuroKit2
\cite{neurokit2021}. \rev{Input: lead II alone, 1000 samples, reduced to a
16-dimensional single-precision vector. R-peak detection and wave delineation were
performed on that one lead. Lead II is the standard rhythm lead, on which RR regularity
and P-wave presence are read. Automated AF detection from a single short lead has been
benchmarked in a dedicated classification challenge \cite{clifford2017af}. A single-lead
definition also lets the feature logic, RR timing and beat morphology, be carried to the
two-lead MIT-BIH beats as the 21-dimensional beat-morphology set, where a twelve-lead
definition would not apply. The arm measures directly the AF signature, RR irregularity
together with P-wave absence.}
\item \textbf{Foundation embeddings} (frozen): mean-pooled hidden states of HuBERT-ECG
(768-d) \cite{hubertecg2024} and the 1024-d pooled features of ECGFounder
\cite{ecgfounder2024}, both used as fixed feature extractors with no fine-tuning.
\rev{Input: all twelve leads. HuBERT-ECG received the first \mbox{5\,s} at
\mbox{100\,Hz}, flattened lead-major into a 6000-sample vector. ECGFounder received the
full \mbox{10\,s} record resampled to 12 by 5000 for its \mbox{500\,Hz} input and
z-scored once over the whole array. Both lead sets are fixed by the published models,
which are defined on the complete twelve-lead record. The pretrained models supply a
fixed ECG feature space, and the question is whether that space places the rhythm
classes in separate regions.}
\end{itemize}

ops.rationale: The Clustering and evaluation subsection gets a label so that the Results can point at it; the heading text is unchanged.
ops.new_text: \subsection{Clustering and evaluation}\label{sec:clustering}

ops.rationale: The 75-word ceiling-and-seeds paragraph is joined with the scaling, K and imbalance paragraph (B0033, deleted by OP011), under one opening sentence that states what both hold, the controls of the evaluation.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each result was read against controls on the representation and on the clustering
set-up. A supervised ceiling bounds how much of the label a probe recovers from the same
features under the same patient-grouped five-fold protocol. We report both a linear probe
(balanced logistic regression) and a non-linear probe (random forest), so that a high
ceiling with a low ARI identifies a geometric rather than an informational failure. Each
configuration was repeated over ten seeds, and the headline contrasts were tested with a
paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across seeds. Because heavy-tailed features can dominate
Euclidean distance, we swept four scalers for feature scaling (Yeo-Johnson power,
standard, quantile and robust) and report power scaling as the default unless stated
otherwise. Each scaler was fitted on the full representation matrix, and any hand-crafted
feature a record left undefined was filled with that feature's cohort median before
scaling. To check that fixing the cluster count to the number of classes does not
flatter the comparison, we also report adjusted mutual information, which is comparable
across cluster counts, for $K$ from 2 to 8. Because the natural SR-to-AF prevalence is
imbalanced, we additionally evaluated on a 9:1 SR:AF subsample.}

ops.rationale: The text of this paragraph now stands, unchanged in wording, at the end of the joined paragraph of OP010.

The fedavg2017 citation now supports only what the source defines, centroid aggregation in the manner of federated averaging (C22); 'standard federated k-means' is gone, and the weighting stays in the later sentence of the paragraph.
ops.new_text:
\rev{To probe deployment under data siloing we used federated $k$-means, with the centroids
aggregated in the manner of federated averaging (FedAvg) \cite{fedavg2017}. The 2\,542 records were partitioned,
patient-grouped, across ten simulated sites, either independently and identically
distributed (IID) or with class proportions drawn from a Dirichlet distribution so that
sites differ sharply in arrhythmia prevalence (non-IID). The Dirichlet concentration was
0.3, applied per class over the ten sites, and any site left holding fewer records than
clusters was dropped. Feature scaling was fitted once on the full representation matrix
before partitioning, so the federation concerns the clustering step alone. Each federated
clustering consisted of fifteen aggregation rounds of three local Lloyd iterations per
site, with the server replacing each centroid by the mean of the site centroids weighted
by the number of records each site assigned to it, and the centroids initialised globally
from two randomly drawn records. Both settings were repeated over ten seeds, with the site
partition and the centroid initialisation redrawn at each seed.} We report the
global ARI relative to centralized clustering of the same representation.

ops.rationale: 4.1 opens with the measured range across representations, without the 'representation more than the algorithm' shape of the Abstract and the Introduction, and the 48-word sentence and the closing list become separate sentences.
ops.new_text:
\rev{On PTB-XL the choice of representation moved the best ARI from 0.008 for the conv-AE
to 0.885 for ECGFounder (Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:heatmap}). Within each of
the two representations that clustered well, the four clusterers other than HDBSCAN moved
it far less, from 0.709 to 0.885 for ECGFounder and from 0.544 to 0.711 for the
hand-crafted features. HDBSCAN, which labels most records as noise, lay below them at
0.137 and 0.060. ECGFounder clustered best (ARI up to 0.885 with $k$-means) and the
hand-crafted features were competitive (0.711 with agglomerative clustering). HuBERT-ECG
was weak (0.195), and the raw and conv-AE pipelines were indistinguishable from a
majority-class assignment (ARI $\approx 0$).}

ops.rationale: The reference to the floor of the p-value points at the subsection that explains it, Clustering and evaluation, in place of the whole Methods section.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Each adjacent contrast between representations under $k$-means favoured the
representation higher in the ordering in every seed, and its paired bootstrap interval
excluded zero. A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the $k$-means seeds confirmed every
adjacent contrast, ECGFounder over hand-crafted ($\Delta = 0.242$, paired bootstrap
interval [0.202, 0.280]), hand-crafted over HuBERT-ECG ($\Delta = 0.470$, [0.424,
0.515]), and HuBERT-ECG over raw ($\Delta = 0.174$, [0.146, 0.203]), at $p = 0.002$. That
value is the floor for ten paired seeds described in Section~\ref{sec:clustering}, so each
contrast also carries two effect sizes. Cliff's delta and the matched-pairs rank-biserial
correlation were both 1.00 on all three: every cross-seed pair and every signed rank
favoured the representation higher in the ordering. The magnitudes are therefore read from
the paired differences and their intervals. Moving only the seed left the $k$-means
partitions almost unchanged, so the spread reported with the results is the
patient-grouped bootstrap given in the caption of Table~\ref{tab:main}, whose intervals
separate every pair of representations except raw-flatten from conv-AE.}

ops.rationale: The K-sweep paragraph closes with what its values show for the comparison, that the three representations above chance kept their order at every K, from the values it already gives.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The ordering does not depend on fixing the cluster count to the number of classes.
With adjusted mutual information for $K$ from 2 to 8, ECGFounder led at every $K$, from
0.825 at $K=2$ to a minimum of 0.441 at $K=7$ and 0.450 at $K=8$. The hand-crafted
features fell monotonically from 0.557 to 0.329, HuBERT-ECG stayed at or below 0.132, and
the raw pipeline never exceeded 0.005. Because the lowest hand-crafted value, 0.329,
stayed above the highest HuBERT-ECG value, 0.132, ECGFounder, the hand-crafted features
and HuBERT-ECG kept that order at every $K$.}

ops.rationale: The reference to the clusterer settings points at the subsection that gives them, Clustering and evaluation, in place of the whole Methods section.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The two foundation models did not behave as one category. ECGFounder clustered
strongly while HuBERT-ECG did not, which matches the report of \cite{lookingbeyond2026}
that some ECG foundation embeddings organise by clinical label and others by dataset.
HDBSCAN labelled most records as noise and underperformed throughout, and spectral
clustering reached an ARI of 0.016 on HuBERT-ECG, against 0.174 with $k$-means on the same
matrix, and 0.001 and 0.000 on the conv-AE and raw flattening (Table~\ref{tab:main}). Both
are reported with the settings of Section~\ref{sec:clustering}, without further tuning.}

ops.rationale: The phrase 'little label information that a linear probe recovers', already given two sentences earlier in this paragraph and again in 4.2, is replaced in the closing sentence by a shorter reference to it.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The conv-AE and raw flattening show two different ways for a representation to fail.
The conv-AE ceiling of 0.678 is what a bottleneck optimised to reconstruct signal energy
retains of a class it was never asked about, and it recovered 0.008. Raw flattening
reached 0.519 against a majority of 0.504, so a linear probe found little label
information in the 1992-dimensional vector. A likely reason is that its coordinates are
amplitudes at fixed sample offsets, and no fixed offset falls on the same part of the
cardiac cycle in two records. A random forest on the same vector reached 0.714, so some
label information remains that a linear probe does not reach. Both rows sat at a
majority-class assignment under all five clusterers, the raw vector for want of linearly
accessible label information and the conv-AE code because it holds more without
arranging it into clusters. Changing the clustering algorithm addresses neither.}

ops.rationale: The conv-AE is named as this study's arm, the raw arm is referred to by its ceiling without restating its reading from 4.1, and the sslclustering2025 citation takes the wording C20 gives.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The supervised ceilings (last column of Table~\ref{tab:main} and Fig.~\ref{fig:sep})
exposed the gap between separability and clusterability. The raw pipeline's linear
ceiling of 0.519 was consistent with its chance-level clustering. The conv-AE was more
separable (0.678) yet still clustered at chance (best ARI 0.008, from Ward agglomerative).
Although properly trained as a reconstruction model, it encoded the class without
organising it into clusters. HuBERT-ECG was the sharpest case, with a ceiling of 0.899 but
an ARI of only 0.195. ECGFounder and the hand-crafted features achieved both high
separability and high clusterability. The discriminative information exists in the weaker
embeddings but does not lie along their dominant axes of variation, consistent with the
separability-versus-clusterability gap reported for self-supervised image encoders
\cite{sslclustering2025}.}

ops.rationale: The raw arm's random-forest value is read once here against its clustering ARI, without restating its comparison with the linear ceiling that 4.1 now gives.
ops.new_text:
\rev{A non-linear probe showed that the gap is not an artefact of a linear one. On the raw
features the random forest reached 0.714 against a clustering ARI of 0.000, so even a
non-linear decoder recovers a label that clustering does not. The same probe gave 0.951 on
the hand-crafted features, 0.983 on ECGFounder and 0.825 on HuBERT-ECG. On the two
representations that clustered well it added little over the linear ceiling, 0.951 against
0.942 for the hand-crafted features and 0.9835 against 0.9831 for ECGFounder, so their
label information is already linearly accessible. For HuBERT-ECG the random forest sat
below the linear ceiling of 0.899, so probe linearity does not account for that gap
either.}

ops.rationale: The degenerate solution's count is stated as the bound the printed fraction gives (1.00 to two decimals on 2 542 records leaves at most 12 outside), and the two closing sentences that restate the Related work point are cut, keeping the 0.89 reference in one shorter sentence, so 4.3 is clearly shorter than 4.4 and 4.5.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The silhouette, an internal index, rewarded a degenerate solution on this cohort.
Raw flattening with agglomerative clustering attained a silhouette of 0.81 while its
largest cluster held all but at most 12 of the 2\,542 records (largest-cluster fraction
1.00 to two decimals) and the ARI was 0.000. The hand-crafted representation, which
recovered the classes (ARI 0.711, balanced clusters), had a \emph{lower} silhouette of
0.28 (Fig.~\ref{fig:trap}). The original project's silhouette of 0.89 arose from the same
artefact.}

ops.rationale: The Feature scaling subsection gets a label so that the Limitations can point at it; the heading text is unchanged.
ops.new_text: \subsection[Feature scaling]{\rev{Feature scaling}}\label{sec:scaling}

ops.rationale: The outlier mechanism behind the fall under robust scaling is hedged as a likely reason, and the unmeasured partition collapse is cut, since the text gives no measure of either.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Feature scaling changed the outcome by a wide margin. For the hand-crafted features
the mean ARI over clusterers was 0.629 under standard scaling and 0.606 under power
scaling, but fell to 0.360 under robust scaling and 0.229 under quantile scaling. The
effect was not confined to the hand-crafted features: ECGFounder's mean ARI dropped from
0.866 (standard) to 0.093 under robust scaling. A likely reason is that robust scaling
leaves heavy arrhythmic tails unbounded, so that a few outliers may dominate Euclidean
distance. A clustering result on these representations therefore needs its scaler
stated, and this study reports power scaling unless stated otherwise.}

ops.rationale: The fourth name of the property, 'the deployability claim', which refers to a claim the paper no longer makes, is replaced by what the cost table adds to the choice between representations.
ops.new_text:
\rev{Table~\ref{tab:cost} states what each representation costs to compute, since the choice
between representations depends on cost as well as on clustering quality. Cost and
clustering quality were ordered against each other: ECGFounder, which clustered best, was
the most expensive per record, fifteen times the hand-crafted extraction, and both
foundation models needed a gigabyte or more of resident memory against \mbox{364\,MB} for
the hand-crafted path, which carries no learned parameters at all. Clustering itself was
negligible everywhere, under \mbox{0.3\,s} for the whole cohort at any of the five
dimensionalities, so the cost of a representation is the cost of extracting it.}

ops.rationale: The 73-word conditional sentence ends at 'the better choice' and its evidence follows in sentences of its own, the imbalance evidence restricted to the one ratio evaluated and the federated retention given through Table fed in a shape that differs from the Conclusion's.
ops.new_text:
\rev{For the PTB-XL rhythm task and the MIT-BIH morphology task, the results support a
decision rule.} If a strong public foundation model can be run on balanced data in the
target 12-lead format, ECGFounder gives the best unsupervised separation here. If the data
are imbalanced or siloed across sites, if interpretability or low dimensionality matters,
or if the leads on hand are not the standard twelve, the 16 hand-crafted features are the
better choice\rev{. On the PTB-XL cohort they were within reach of ECGFounder on balanced
data (0.711 against 0.885). They led it at the 9:1 ratio (0.265 against 0.063), the one
imbalanced setting evaluated. Under non-IID federation their retention was 0.92 against
0.69 for ECGFounder (Table~\ref{tab:fed}). The cost comparison of Table~\ref{tab:cost}
points the same way: the representation that held up better under both stressors is also
the lower-cost one to compute. The lead constraint is concrete. The two foundation models
we test could not be applied to the 2-lead MIT-BIH beats, whereas the hand-crafted feature
logic carried to them as the 21-dimensional beat-morphology set.}

ops.rationale: The comparison names the hand-crafted features for PTB-XL and the beat-morphology features for MIT-BIH, and the 73-word paragraph closes with what the two pipelines' result means for the original project and for the decision rule above it.
ops.new_text:
\rev{On PTB-XL the raw and conv-AE pipelines were indistinguishable from a majority-class
assignment under all five clusterers. On MIT-BIH, evaluated with three clusterers, the
conv-AE reached at most 0.127 and the raw beat window at most 0.049, against 0.783 for the
beat-morphology features. On both tasks these two pipelines recovered far less of the
class structure than the hand-crafted features on PTB-XL and the beat-morphology features
on MIT-BIH. The raw arm reproduces the input of the original project's design. Its
PTB-XL result therefore gives that project's conclusion, that the difficulty lies in processing the
raw signal, in chance-corrected terms. The decision rule above therefore chooses only
between ECGFounder and the hand-crafted features.}

ops.rationale: The lookingbeyond2026 citation names the one model it reports to separate by clinical label, ECG-FM (C23), without the 'rather than by dataset' contrast, and the lead reason is pointed at the Representations subsection.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The foundation-model arm is limited in its input rate and in the models it holds.
ECGFounder expects 500\,Hz input, and because the 500\,Hz release could not be obtained in
full for this study, the main benchmark embeds the 100\,Hz cohort upsampled to the expected
length. A comparison on a 300-record subset gave ECGFounder an ARI of 0.909 with the
upsampled 100\,Hz input and 0.896 with the native 500\,Hz input. The upsampled input may
therefore raise ECGFounder's ARI by about 0.013 on that subset, which is small against its
$k$-means lead of 0.242 over the hand-crafted features. We evaluate two foundation models.
Other foundation models, including ECG-FM, which the closest benchmark reports to separate
by clinical label \cite{lookingbeyond2026}, are not included, and
Section~\ref{sec:discussion} sets out how this bounds the conclusions. The MIT-BIH arm has
no foundation-model row, for the lead reason given in Section~\ref{sec:representations}.}

ops.rationale: The reference to the scaling results points at the Feature scaling subsection in place of the whole Results section.
ops.new_text:
\rev{The federated study simulates ten sites within one dataset. Its only control on
heterogeneity is the Dirichlet concentration, which moves class prevalence across sites
and nothing else, and the spread that alone produces is already wide: over the ten redrawn
non-IID partitions ECGFounder ranges from chance to 0.881, while the hand-crafted features
stay between 0.455 and 0.643. Feature scaling in the simulation is fitted on statistics
pooled over all sites, which a real federation would not have, and
Section~\ref{sec:scaling} shows that feature scaling changes the results by a wide margin.
Device vendor, lead placement, population case mix and local labelling practice also differ
between hospitals and are absent from the simulation. Settling their effect needs ECG
records held at several institutions, clustered under a federated protocol with the site
of origin retained as a variable, which was not available for this study.}

ops.rationale: The Conclusion restricts the imbalance statement to the 9:1 ratio, the one imbalanced setting evaluated, in place of the general 'under class imbalance'.
ops.new_text:
\rev{For unsupervised arrhythmia structure in the ECG, the spread of ARI across
representations exceeded the spread across clustering algorithms within each
representation that clustered well, and chance-corrected external evaluation was required
to see it. This held on the two tasks evaluated here: SR-versus-AF rhythm separation in
PTB-XL and N-vs-V beat morphology in MIT-BIH. On balanced PTB-XL data ECGFounder,
pretrained on more than ten million recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}, leads. At a 9:1
SR:AF ratio, 16 interpretable hand-crafted features overtake it, and under simulated
federation across ten heterogeneous sites they are the more predictable of the two,
retaining 0.92 of their centralized ARI against 0.69 and never falling below 0.455 over the
ten site draws. On PTB-XL the raw and conv-AE pipelines sit at chance under all five
clusterers. Internal indices and feature scaling are not neutral and must be reported.
Whether these results hold for multi-class arrhythmia cohorts, for other foundation models
and for a real multi-institution federation is open.}

\section*{Code and data availability}
\rev{PTB-XL \cite{ptbxl2020}, used in its version 1.0.3 release,} and the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (version 1.0.0) \cite{mitbih2001} are public
on PhysioNet. The benchmark code, with the exact cohort
definitions, is available at \url{https://github.com/TheAxeC/ecg-representation-clustering}.
